## 6. Bundled binaries

Programs shipped next to the server. Their license texts ship alongside the binaries.

| Name | Version | License | Component / platforms | Source | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|

## 7. Downloaded on your computer by the component manager, not distributed with LectureFlow / 由组件管理器在你的电脑上下载、不随本程序分发的组件

These Python packages are not part of the LectureFlow installer or of any LectureFlow download. When you install a component that needs them, the component manager downloads them on your computer from PyPI (or the mirror you chose), pinned by the component's lock file, into that component's own Python environment, which runs in a separate process. Their licenses, listed here, are between you and their authors; LectureFlow does not publish offline component archives that contain them. LectureFlow's combination with these libraries is covered by the additional permission under section 7 of the GNU AGPL in `LICENSE-EXCEPTION.md`; that permission does not change their licenses, and LectureFlow still does not distribute them.

这些 Python 包不包含在 LectureFlow 安装包或任何 LectureFlow 下载中。安装需要它们的组件时，组件管理器按锁定文件从 PyPI（或你选择的镜像）把它们下载到你的电脑上，装入该组件独立的 Python 环境，并在独立进程中运行。它们的许可证如下；LectureFlow 不发布包含这些包的离线组件压缩包。LectureFlow 与这些库的组合使用依据 `LICENSE-EXCEPTION.md` 中 GNU AGPL 第 7 条的附加许可；该附加许可不改变它们的许可证，LectureFlow 也仍然不分发它们。

## 9. Upstreams reimplemented from their protocol, no code copied / 参照其协议重新实现、未复制代码的上游

LectureFlow contains no code from these projects. Parts of LectureFlow were written to follow their protocol; their copyright and license notices are kept here, and their license texts are in Appendix A.

LectureFlow 不包含这些项目的代码。下列部分参照它们的协议重新编写；这里保留其版权与许可声明，许可证全文见附录 A。

### google-colab-cli 0.7.5

- License: Apache-2.0
- Copyright 2026 Google LLC
- Source: https://pypi.org/project/google-colab-cli/0.7.5/
- Read: google_colab_cli-0.7.5-py3-none-any.whl (sha256 2b303ed21ebd6da829f80d506224a6cd4f0e62d506fb373166d06a0532e516a9), read 2026-10-24, not installed, not run
- Referenced for: The protocol between the Colab CLI and the Colab service (ADC credentials and scopes, /tun/m assign / unassign / assignments / ccu-info, XSRF and proxy tokens, Jupyter Contents API and kernel execution on the runtime).
- Used by: internal/colab (Go)
- Changes: Reimplemented in Go from the protocol; no upstream source was copied or translated line by line. Differences from upstream (queueing with back-off on 412, narrowed refresh scopes, token revocation, chunked uploads, own client agent string, no console/ssh) are listed in internal/colab/UPSTREAM.md.
- Details: `internal/colab/UPSTREAM.md`
- License text: google_colab_cli-0.7.5.dist-info/licenses/LICENSE in the wheel (the Apache-2.0 text; the copyright line is from the source file headers)

## 10. Programs downloaded from their vendor on your computer, not distributed with LectureFlow / 由组件管理器从官方下载到你的电脑、不随本程序分发的程序

When you install one of these components, the component manager downloads the vendor's own archive from the vendor's server, checks its SHA-256 against the component manifest and unpacks it; LectureFlow runs it as a separate program. It is not part of the LectureFlow installer or of any LectureFlow download, and LectureFlow publishes no offline archive of it. Its license, listed here, is between you and its vendor; the parts the vendor bundles in its archive keep their own licenses (see the note and the license files inside the installed tool).

安装这些组件时，组件管理器从官方服务器下载官方压缩包，按组件清单核对 SHA-256 后解压，LectureFlow 把它作为独立程序运行。它们不包含在 LectureFlow 安装包或任何 LectureFlow 下载中，LectureFlow 也不发布它们的离线压缩包。其许可证如下，由你与其发布者之间约定；官方压缩包内附带的部分各自遵循其许可证（见备注与安装目录中的许可证文件）。

| Name | Version | License | Platforms | Source | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| gcloud | 590.0.1 | Apache-2.0 | darwin-arm64 windows-x64 | https://docs.cloud.google.com/sdk/docs/downloads-versioned-archives | Google Cloud CLI 590.0.1 (Windows: with its bundled Python 3.14; macOS: runs on the python component). Downloaded from Google (dl.google.com) on the user's computer by the component manager and run as a separate program; not part of the LectureFlow installer and never put into an offline archive. The Google Cloud CLI is Apache-2.0 unless an alternate license file says otherwise; the Python bundled in the Windows archive (PSF-2.0, with the Microsoft C runtime DLLs) and the third-party libraries under lib/third_party and platform/ keep their own licenses (license files inside the installed tool). On Windows the component leaves out six directories of API clients and test data that LectureFlow never uses and whose paths are too long for Windows (packaging/components/README.md, Tools). |

form or as a compiled binary, for any purpose, commercial or non-commercial,
and by any means.

The previous paragraph applies to the deliverable code and documentation in
SQLite - those parts of the SQLite library that you actually bundle and ship
with a larger application. Some scripts used as part of the build process (for
example the "configure" scripts generated by autoconf) might fall under other
open-source licenses. Nothing from these build scripts ever reaches the final
deliverable SQLite library, however, and so the licenses associated with those
scripts should not be a factor in assessing your rights to copy and use the
SQLite library.

All of the deliverable code in SQLite has been written from scratch. No code
has been taken from other projects or from the open internet. Every line of
code can be traced back to its original author, and all of those authors have
public domain dedications on file. So the SQLite code base is clean and is
uncontaminated with licensed code from other projects.

A. HISTORY OF THE SOFTWARE
==========================

Python was created in the early 1990s by Guido van Rossum at Stichting
Mathematisch Centrum (CWI, see http://www.cwi.nl) in the Netherlands
as a successor of a language called ABC.  Guido remains Python's
principal author, although it includes many contributions from others.

In 1995, Guido continued his work on Python at the Corporation for
National Research Initiatives (CNRI, see http://www.cnri.reston.va.us)
in Reston, Virginia where he released several versions of the
software.

In May 2000, Guido and the Python core development team moved to
BeOpen.com to form the BeOpen PythonLabs team.  In October of the same
year, the PythonLabs team moved to Digital Creations, which became
Zope Corporation.  In 2001, the Python Software Foundation (PSF, see
https://www.python.org/psf/) was formed, a non-profit organization
created specifically to own Python-related Intellectual Property.
Zope Corporation was a sponsoring member of the PSF.

All Python releases are Open Source (see http://www.opensource.org for
the Open Source Definition).  Historically, most, but not all, Python
releases have also been GPL-compatible; the table below summarizes
the various releases.

    Release         Derived     Year        Owner       GPL-

Footnotes:

(1) GPL-compatible doesn't mean that we're distributing Python under
    the GPL.  All Python licenses, unlike the GPL, let you distribute
    a modified version without making your changes open source.  The
    GPL-compatible licenses make it possible to combine Python with

## Appendix B: Where the other license texts are

- Python packages: `*.dist-info/licenses/` (or `*.dist-info/LICENSE*`) inside each installed component; upstream at the source links above.
- Python packages whose wheel carries no license file (for example mlx-whisper): the text is reproduced in Appendix A from a copy kept in `packaging/licenses/texts/`, pinned to an upstream commit (see the package note in section 4).
- Upstreams reimplemented from their protocol (section 9): copies of their license files are kept in `packaging/licenses/texts/` and reproduced in Appendix A.
- Models: the license file or model card of each source repository listed in section 5.
- Programs downloaded from their vendor (section 10): the license files inside the installed tool (`components/{id}/{version}/tool/`; for the Google Cloud CLI its `LICENSE` and the license files of the parts it bundles).
- Bundled binaries: the license files shipped next to each binary (section 6).
- Electron: `LICENSE` and `LICENSES.chromium.html` in the application directory.
